concept.title: The classification as SKOS
concept.shortdesc: Each dimension is also published as a SKOS concept scheme, so that other systems can read the draft categories and their hierarchy without scraping these pages.

conbody.note: The SKOS describes a draft. Its concepts carry the draft identifiers of one run, which change whenever the pipeline is re-run. Do not use them as stable identifiers.

section.title: What is published
section.p: When the website is built with the SKOS option on, the build writes one file pair for each dimension, in two syntaxes with the same content:
Each file holds a skos:ConceptScheme. The groups are its top concepts and the categories are the concepts beneath them.

section.title: How the pages map to SKOS

strow.stentry: A skos:ConceptScheme, with the dimension's title
A group, as an entry in the subject scheme
A skos:Concept that is a top concept of the scheme
A category, nested under its group
A skos:Concept with skos:broader its group (and the group skos:narrower it)
skos:notation, and the fragment of the concept's address

section.title: What is not in the SKOS yet
section.p: The concept pages carry more than the SKOS files do. The publishing plugin reads names, definitions, notations and the hierarchy from the subject scheme. It does not yet read these from concept pages, so they appear on the pages but not in the files:

ul.li: the everyday search phrases, which would be alternative labels (skos:altLabel)
the boundaries between categories, which would be skos:related links
matches to other lists, such as the Local Government Association's standard lists (skos:exactMatch and skos:closeMatch). No such mapping has been made for this draft.

section.p: The plugin's design records reading concept topics as SKOS concepts as planned work, not built.

section.title: Building it
section.p: The SKOS files need the site's address, because every concept's identifier is an address. Build with the plugin's SKOS switch on and the site address set:
Replace the example address with the one the site will be published at. The build script build-classification.ps1 does this and takes the address as a parameter.
The website's pages also carry machine-readable descriptions in their heads when the metadata option is set to full. The PDF carries the standard document properties only: it does not carry the SKOS.
